narrative:
## Context

We use 5 systems:
1. Oracle Field Services - for internally delivered work
2. Oracle Unifier - for externally delivered work
3. GE Electric Office - for linear asset data
4. IBM Maximo - for non-linear asset data
5. RRD - for work volume reporting to support regulatory reporting 

## Problem

We have no mechanism to manage changes to asset data, captured in Oracle Field Service, or Unifier (using standard 'Asset Data Capture Forms'), and drive changes through to systems of record. (GE Electric Office, IBM Maximo, RRD)

## Proposal

A PaaS/Low-Code system built on MS PowerPlatform that allows automated and manual (human in the loop) checks.
Interfaces from work execution/delivery systems to PaaS
Interfaces from PaaS to system of records.

requirements.title: 30.5a Completed Work and Asset Data Demand Control
requirements.description:
This feature provides a controlled way to identify completed work that should enter the Asset Data process and establish what Asset Data and supporting evidence are expected from it.

For internally delivered work, the process will identify relevant activities that have reached the agreed operational-completion point in OFFS. For contractor-delivered work, it will identify relevant work where the Project Manager has marked the information as ready for ADT in Unifier.

In both routes, FA5 will use the readiness information and available work context to create a traceable Asset Data expectation. This expectation will remain visible until the required information has been received, a legitimate exemption has been agreed, or the matter has reached another explicit outcome.

The feature follows a pull-based model. It does not require the upstream user or Project Manager to push a Green Label pack into an FA5 system.

This feature establishes that Asset Data should exist and what is broadly expected. Accessing, associating and reconciling the detailed artefacts is covered by the subsequent FA5 information-preparation feature.

requirements.title: 30.5b Asset Data Information Preparation
requirements.description:
This feature provides the information needed to process completed work through the Asset Data and Green Label journey.

For internally delivered work, FA5 will access the relevant outputs made available through the OFFS route. For contractor-delivered work, FA5 will access the information that has been marked ready for ADT in Unifier.

The feature will associate the available ADCFs, marked-up designs, supporting evidence and work information with the correct originating activity. It will compare what has been received with the Asset Data expectation established for that work and identify whether the information is complete, partial, missing, duplicated, superseded, mismatched, inaccessible or legitimately exempt.

The outcome will be a coherent and traceable information set that can proceed into pre-review quality assessment. Where the required information cannot be prepared, the exception will remain visible and owned rather than disappearing from the process.

The feature does not assume that all information must be copied into a single physical Green Label pack. The high-level architecture may support retrieval, controlled references, temporary staging, a combined view or an appropriate combination of these approaches.

requirements.title: 30.5c Pre-Review Asset Data Quality Assessment
30.5d Asset Data Workload Control
requirements.description:
This feature provides a controlled view of Asset Data work that is ready for action or remains outstanding at another stage of the journey.

It allows ADT managers and operators to see what work is available, what needs attention, who currently owns it and what is preventing it from progressing. It covers work that is ready for ADT review as well as items waiting for missing information, clarification, correction or technical support.

The feature supports the allocation and prioritisation of work using relevant information such as age, readiness, work context, identified quality findings and expected complexity. It maintains visibility when the next action sits with a Project Manager, work team, contractor or FA7 support role.

Corrected or resubmitted information remains connected to the existing work and can return to the appropriate operator or team with its previous context intact. It should not automatically appear as an unrelated new job requiring the earlier assessment to be repeated from the beginning.

This feature controls the current operational workload. The enduring identity, complete history and audit trail of each Asset Data case are covered by the separate FA5 case lifecycle and traceability feature.

The feature does not assume that one system or one physical backlog will manage every FA5 and FA6 state. KDD 2.3.7 will inform whether FA5 processing, work ready for ADT and active FA6 work are managed through one shared capability or through linked views.

requirements.title: 30.6a Human As-Built Assessment
requirements.description:
This feature enables an Asset Data Team member to assess the information returned from completed work and determine the as-built position.

The ADT member will review the relevant forms, marked-up design, supporting evidence, work context, available design baseline and FA5 quality findings together. They will use professional judgement to understand what was built, identify any material difference from the proposed design and record the affected design, network or asset information.

The feature distinguishes a genuine as-built variation from information that is missing, unclear, contradictory or incorrect. Where substantive information cannot be understood reliably, the ADT member will identify that clarification, correction or specialist input is required rather than inferring the answer.

Material as-built variations are expected to remain human-identified because they are generally represented through mark-ups on drawings or PDFs that cannot currently be assumed to support reliable automated interpretation.

Where the appropriate approved design and structured Asset Data are available, the assessment should allow ADT to reuse that information rather than reconstructing the proposed change from the beginning. The feature does not itself manage the subsequent clarification, correction, referral, acceptance or rejection process.

requirements.title: 30.6b Asset Data Resolution and Decision Management
requirements.description:
This feature enables an authorised Asset Data Team member to decide how an Asset Data case should progress following human assessment.

Where information is unclear, incomplete or incorrect, the ADT member can request clarification or correction from the responsible work team, contractor or Project Manager. Where specialist or technical input is required, the case can be referred through the appropriate route. Where the information cannot proceed, the ADT member can formally reject it. Where the information is acceptable, the ADT member can approve it for the applicable EO update.

Clarification, correction, referral and rejection will be managed as controlled parts of the existing Asset Data case. Each action will identify the issue, the information affected, the action required and the party responsible for responding. The case will remain visible and owned while action is outstanding.

Substantive missing or unclear information should be provided or corrected by the originating party. ADT should not infer the intended answer. An ADT member may correct a genuinely minor typographical error where this is proportionate and within their agreed authority, but the correction and its basis must remain consistent with the required audit and management-information controls.

When revised information is returned, it will remain linked to the original case, issue and submission cycle. The ADT member will be able to see what changed and continue the earlier assessment without treating the returned information as an unrelated new job. Relevant FA5 checks can be repeated where the correction affects an earlier finding.

This feature manages the human decision and the resulting action. It stops when the case has an authorised next outcome, including acceptance for update. Applying accepted information through EO and confirming the downstream Maximo synchronisation are covered by the subsequent FA6 feature.

requirements.title: 30.6c Accepted Asset Data Update and Completion
30.5e Asset Data Case Lifecycle and Traceability
requirements.description:
This feature maintains the identity, status and history of an Asset Data case from the point at which completed work creates an Asset Data obligation through to its final operational outcome.

The case will remain linked to the originating work, the Asset Data expected and received, the relevant forms and design evidence, FA5 quality findings, ADT assessment, clarification and correction cycles, decisions, the accepted EO update and the resulting FA7 integration outcome.

Users will be able to understand what has happened to an Asset Data case without reconstructing its history from separate systems, reports, emails, Teams messages or individual knowledge. The case will show the current business position, who or which route is responsible for the next action, and the significant events and decisions that led to that position.

Where information is corrected or resubmitted, the revised information will remain part of the original case context. Earlier findings, requests, responses and decisions will not be lost or overwritten. Where the same originating work requires more than one submission or correction cycle, those cycles will remain distinguishable while retaining their relationship to the same work.

The feature will maintain the business relationship to the EO update and the outcome supplied by FA7. It will not duplicate FA7 technical logs, integration monitoring or reconciliation. It will retain or reference the integration outcome needed to understand whether the Asset Data case completed successfully, remains pending or requires further action.

This feature provides the common lifecycle and traceability model used across FA5 and FA6. It does not assume that every part of the case must be held in one system. KDD 2.3.7 will determine where the authoritative case and status are maintained and which participating systems hold reflected information.

requirements.title: 30.6d PQS Reconciliation and Asset Data Assurance
30.6e Lost, Found and Modified Discrepancy Resolution

recommendations.recommendation: **Narrative strength:** Clear, well-grounded context with five systems named. Problem and proposed solution are explicit. Structure supports downstream analysis.

**Requirements 30.5a, 30.5b, 30.5c** — Each combines multiple obligations. Example: 30.5a conflates 'identifying completed work,' 'establishing expectation,' and 'pull-based model.' Consider splitting each into focused, single-statement requirements for testability.

**Requirements 30.5d, 30.6a–e** — Narrative is rich but lengthy (some >300 words). Consider distilling each requirement title to a single verb + object, with detail moved to acceptance criteria or a separate design spec.

**Acronyms & domain terms** — FA5, FA6, EO, ADT, PQS, and LFM are used throughout requirements without a glossary. For a business audience unfamiliar with your domain, add a footnoted glossary or expand first mention.

**Acceptance criteria** — Requirements describe *what* will be delivered but lack testable acceptance criteria (e.g., 'ADT can view workload in <3 seconds' or 'case history remains linked across 5 correction cycles'). Consider adding measurable pass/fail conditions.

recommendations-summary:
- **Overall:** Narrative and context are clear and well-grounded. Problem, systems, and proposal are explicit.
- **Requirements atomicity:** Most requirements conflate multiple obligations (e.g., 30.5a combines demand control, pull-model, and expectation). Break into single statements.
- **Requirements length:** Some exceed 300 words; distil titles and move detail to acceptance criteria.
- **Domain terminology:** FA5, FA6, EO, ADT, PQS, LFM used without glossary—clarify for business readers.
- **Acceptance criteria:** Requirements lack testable, measurable pass/fail conditions. Add explicit criteria.

impact-assessment.finding: **Application Domains & Platforms** (`APP-DAP`) — Five systems identified as work execution sources (Oracle Field Services, Oracle Unifier), systems of record (GE Electric Office, IBM Maximo) and reporting endpoint (RRD). Proposed MS PowerPlatform PaaS is not yet mapped to any defined application platform or domain.
impact-assessment.impact: APP-DAP must account for all five source/target systems and the new PaaS platform. Without platform mapping, downstream application catalogue (`APP-CAT`), process-to-platform (`APP-PRO-DAP`), and data-to-platform (`APP-DAP-DAC`) matrices cannot be populated or validated.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Create or update `APP-DAP` to define: (1) the five existing systems as platforms or platform groupings; (2) the MS PowerPlatform as a new application domain/platform with 'integration engine' or 'data broker' role. Update `APP-CAT` if physical applications (product versions/instances) vary.
impact-assessment.rationale: The decision mandates interfaces and data flow between multiple systems. Platforms must be explicitly defined and connected before integration patterns and data mappings can be validated. This is the foundational step for subsequent matrix updates.

impact-assessment.finding: **Interface Catalogue** (`INT-IFC`) — Decision specifies three interface directions: (1) from work systems to PaaS; (2) from PaaS to systems of record; (3) via PaaS-managed quality checks and workload control. These interfaces are logical and must be mapped.
impact-assessment.impact: INT-IFC must enumerate the logical channels between Oracle Field Services ↔ PaaS, Oracle Unifier ↔ PaaS, PaaS ↔ GE Electric Office, PaaS ↔ IBM Maximo, and PaaS ↔ RRD. Without these, integration dependencies and data-flow governance cannot be documented. The Interface Wiring Diagram (`INT-WRD`) cannot be rendered.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Populate `INT-IFC` with at least five logical interfaces representing the data/control flows listed above. For each, specify direction (request/response, push/pull, event-driven) and whether it is synchronous or asynchronous. Update or create `INT-DAC-IFC` to map the data concepts flowing across each interface.
impact-assessment.rationale: Integration is central to the decision. Explicit interface definition is required to validate data consistency, detect circular dependencies, and communicate integration architecture to delivery teams. The logical interface layer is independent of technology choice (e.g., REST, message queue, etc.).

impact-assessment.finding: **Data Domains & Concepts** (`DAT-DAC`) — Decision references 'Asset Data' and 'Asset Data Capture Forms' but does not enumerate the data entities or subject areas. Data provenance (source systems), transformation (PaaS checks), and destination (systems of record) are not formally specified.
impact-assessment.impact: DAT-DAC must define the data subject areas and entities involved in the asset data process (e.g., 'Asset Details', 'Work Completion Evidence', 'Quality Findings', 'Correction Cycles'). Process-to-data mapping (`DAT-PRO-DAC`: CRUD matrix) and application-to-data mapping (`APP-DAP-DAC`: systems of record) depend on this foundation.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Create or update `DAT-DAC` to define conceptual data entities and subject areas for: asset attributes, asset history, quality findings, correction metadata, traceability information, and any domain-specific entities (e.g., PQS markers, LFM discrepancies). Cross-reference with existing Asset Data domain language in your baseline.
impact-assessment.rationale: Data governance and integration success depend on agreed, explicit definitions. The decision emphasises traceability and corrections—both require data models that preserve history and relationships. A formal data domain ensures consistency across work systems, PaaS, and systems of record.

impact-assessment.finding: **Business Processes** (`BUS-PRO`) — Decision references 'asset data process' (multiple stages: identification, preparation, quality assessment, workload management, human assessment, resolution, completion) but does not map these to existing Level 1/2 business processes or define the process hierarchy.
impact-assessment.impact: BUS-PRO must capture the 'asset data process' (or multiple sub-processes) as Level 1 or Level 2 activities. This is the foundation for mapping processes to applications (`APP-PRO-DAP`), processes to data (`DAT-PRO-DAC`: which activities create/read/update/delete asset data), and tracing user journeys (`SOL-PRF`: process flows across applications).
impact-assessment.recommendation: Update or add to `BUS-PRO` a new process tree capturing the multi-stage asset data journey: identify work completion → establish data expectation → prepare information → quality assess → assign workload → human review → resolve/decide → update systems of record → complete case. Define at least L1 (asset data process) and L2 (each major stage) levels.
impact-assessment.rationale: The decision is process-centric: it defines a governance workflow with human gates, quality checks, and state transitions. Representing this as a formal process enables process-to-data (`DAT-PRO-DAC`) and process-to-application (`APP-PRO-DAP`) mapping, which drives integration validation and impact analysis for future decisions.

impact-assessment.finding: **Data Guardrails** (`DAT-GRD`) — Requirements reference mandatory controls: traceability, audit trails, linked context, correction history, exemptions, dispositions, and role-based decision rights. These are non-negotiable constraints but are not yet codified as guardrails.
impact-assessment.impact: DAT-GRD must define guardrails enforcing: (1) immutable audit trails for all asset data decisions and changes; (2) traceability linking asset data cases to originating work and downstream updates; (3) role-based access and decision authorities (ADT member, Project Manager, contractor, etc.); (4) mandatory correction and re-link logic preventing orphaned submissions. These are essential governance rules.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Define `DAT-GRD` entries for: mandatory traceability (links must survive corrections), audit-trail immutability, role-based decision rights (who may approve/reject), exemption management, and case-lifecycle continuity. Reference specific requirements (e.g., 30.6b for resolution roles, 30.5e for traceability).
impact-assessment.rationale: The decision mandates 'controlled' processes, 'visible and owned' exceptions, and audit/traceability. These are governance rules, not just features. Guardrails ensure compliance, auditability, and prevent future architectural drift toward looser controls.

impact-assessment.finding: **Solution-layer diagrams** — Decision describes system flows (work execution systems ↔ PaaS ↔ systems of record), information flows (asset data, quality findings, corrections), and user journeys (ADT workload, review, decision, update). These are at solution (logical) layer but not yet formally diagrammed.
impact-assessment.impact: Solution-layer artefacts (`SOL-SYF`: system flows, `SOL-INF`: information flows) should be created to visualize the multi-system interactions. Without these, delivery teams must infer the flow from requirements, increasing integration risk.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Create or update `SOL-SYF` (system flows) showing the three main flows: (1) work completion identification (OFFS/Unifier → PaaS); (2) information preparation and quality assessment (PaaS orchestration); (3) approved update application (PaaS → EO → Maximo). Create `SOL-INF` (information flows) showing asset data, quality findings, and correction metadata movement. Optionally add `SOL-PRF` (process flows) showing asset-data process execution across applications.
impact-assessment.rationale: Diagram artefacts make complex multi-system interactions visible and communicable. They are input to delivery design and testing strategy. They also provide early error detection (e.g., circular data flows, missing transformations).

impact-assessment.finding: **Gap: Application-to-Data matrix** (`APP-DAP-DAC`) — Decision implies data mastery: which system is the system of record for asset data (GE Electric Office for linear, IBM Maximo for non-linear), but this is not formally mapped. The PaaS role (intermediary, transformer, temporary holder) is ambiguous.
impact-assessment.impact: APP-DAP-DAC must clarify the data mastery model: which application is system of record (SoR) for which data concept; which applications are consumers; whether PaaS holds temporary/staging copies or references. This affects sync strategy, correction routing, and audit.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Populate `APP-DAP-DAC` matrix: rows = APP-DAP platforms (OFFS, Unifier, PaaS, GE EO, Maximo, RRD); columns = DAT-DAC data entities. For each cell, mark 'SoR' (system of record), 'Consumer', or 'Temporary'. Example: GE Electric Office = SoR for 'Linear Asset Details'; Maximo = SoR for 'Non-Linear Asset Details'; PaaS = Temporary for 'Prepared Information Set'.
impact-assessment.rationale: Data mastery (system-of-record mapping) is critical for integration governance. It drives correction/sync routing, audit responsibility, and conflict resolution. The decision's multi-system scope makes this explicit definition essential.

impact-assessment.finding: **Scope validity** — ADR narrative does not explicitly state whether the asset data management system applies only to the baseline transition or if it shapes future target states. Architecture version scope is not documented.
impact-assessment.impact: If the decision is scoped to baseline only, no impact on future transitions. If it establishes architectural baseline for subsequent transitions (2026-Q2, etc.), all future instances must honour these integration patterns and data governance rules. Scope ambiguity can lead to divergent implementations.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Clarify in decision metadata or a separate ADR note whether this decision's integration patterns, data domain, process definitions, and guardrails apply to all future transitions or baseline only. If baseline-only, document transition-specific overrides or evolutions as new ADRs.
impact-assessment.rationale: Architecture decisions must state their temporal and organisational scope to guide future decisions and prevent contradictions. Unclear scope is a source of later rework and inconsistency.

impact-assessment-summary:
- **Overall impact:** Decision introduces a multi-system asset data governance workflow with complex integration and data transformation. Six core architecture artefacts (APP-DAP, INT-IFC, DAT-DAC, BUS-PRO, DAT-GRD, SOL-layer diagrams) require definition or updates.
- **Critical gaps:** No application platform definitions for five existing systems + PaaS; no formal interface catalogue; data entity and process hierarchies not yet modelled.
- **Data governance:** Requires explicit guardrails (traceability, audit trails, role-based decision rights, correction lifecycle) to enforce the controlled, auditable process described in requirements.
- **Systems of record:** APP-DAP-DAC matrix needed to clarify data mastery (which system owns which asset data type) and resolve temporary-staging vs persistent-storage model for PaaS.
- **Scope ambiguity:** No indication whether decision applies to baseline only or future transitions; clarify to prevent downstream contradiction.

referential-integrity.finding: No existing catalogues in scope for referential integrity check. The ADR narrative and impact assessment propose new artefact definitions (APP-DAP, INT-IFC, DAT-DAC, BUS-PRO, DAT-GRD, solution diagrams) but do not modify existing catalogues. The `adc/baseline` architecture contains no domain instances yet.
referential-integrity.impact: No referential integrity violations are possible. Referential integrity checks become applicable only after the proposed artefacts are created and populated with data.
referential-integrity.recommendation: Once proposed artefacts are created and catalogues are populated (via future ADRs or implementation), run a new referential integrity check to validate cross-references within and between catalogues.
referential-integrity.rationale: Referential integrity checks validate existing data. A baseline architecture with no catalogues instantiated has no references to validate. This finding records that the check passed (no violations) because there was no data to check.

referential-integrity-summary:
- **Referential integrity status:** ✓ Passed (no violations).
- **Reason:** ADR proposes new artefacts; no existing catalogues modified.
- **Data scope:** The `adc/baseline` architecture contains no domain instances yet.
- **Next step:** Re-run referential integrity after proposed artefacts are created and populated.
